confirmedFacts.claim: PAN-OS REST API getting-started docs recommend a voluntary client-side concurrency cap: 'For performance considerations, limit the number of concurrent API calls to five. The suggested limit ensures that there is no performance impact to the firewall web interface as the management plane web server handles requests from both the API and the web interface. Limits may vary depending on the type of request. The limit may be higher depending on requests.'
confirmedFacts.evidence: For performance considerations, limit the number of concurrent API calls to five. The suggested limit ensures that there is no performance impact to the firewall web interface as the management plane web server handles requests from both the API and the web interface. Limits may vary depending on the type of request. The limit may be higher depending on requests.

confirmedFacts.claim: The official PAN-OS REST API Error Codes reference page (numeric codes 1-16: canceled, unknown, bad request, gateway timeout, not found, conflict, forbidden, resource exhausted, failed precondition, aborted/concurrency, out of range, not implemented, internal error, service unavailable, unauthorized) contains NO entry for HTTP 429 and NO mention of a Retry-After header. Verified by fetching the raw page HTML directly and confirming the only '429' occurrences in the file are SVG glyph path coordinates and font hint-table numbers, not textual content.
confirmedFacts.evidence: 1 canceled | 2 unknown internal server error | 3 bad request | 4 gateway timeout | 5 not found | 6 conflict | 7 forbidden | 16 unauthorized | 8 resource exhausted | 9 failed precondition | 10 aborted (concurrency) | 11 out of range | 12 not implemented | 13 internal server error | 14 service unavailable | 15 internal server error (data loss) -- no 429/Retry-After entry anywhere in the table or page text

confirmedFacts.claim: The PAN-OS XML API 'Retrieve Logs' documentation (the async job model used for log pulls) describes the poll-until-finished workflow (action=get&job-id=<id> until status is FIN) but states no recommended polling interval and makes no mention of rate limiting, 429, or throttling.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Page describes creating a job then polling action=get&job-id=<id> until status=FIN; no polling-interval recommendation and no rate-limit/429/throttling language present.

confirmedFacts.claim: PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python (the official Python SDK wrapping the XML/REST APIs) has zero references to '429', 'retry', or 'backoff' anywhere in its repository -- confirmed via three separate GitHub code searches scoped to that repo, each returning 0 matching files.
confirmedFacts.evidence: GitHub in-repo search for q=429 -> 'Your search did not match any code' (0 files); same for q=retry and q=backoff.

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python (github.com/kevinsteves/pan-python), the lower-level XML API client historically wrapped by pan-os-python, has NO handling of HTTP 429 or rate-limit responses in its xapi.py source. Its error handling only distinguishes URLError/ssl.CertificateError and raises PanXapiError; it implements no retry loop and no backoff. It does define a module-level default job-status polling interval of 0.5 seconds (_job_query_interval) used by commit()/log()/report() while waiting for an async job to finish -- this is a client-chosen convenience default, not a value published in Palo Alto's own docs.
confirmedFacts.evidence: _job_query_interval = 0.5; polling loop does time.sleep(interval) checking for job status 'FIN'; exception handling covers URLError (with .code) and ssl.CertificateError only -- no 429/backoff branch.

confirmedFacts.claim: PaloAltoNetworks/pango (the Go SDK underlying terraform-provider-panos) builds its HTTP client as a plain `http.Client{Transport: c.Transport}` in client.go with no retry wrapper, no CheckRetry callback, and no RetryMax/RetryWaitMin/RetryWaitMax fields -- confirmed by reading the raw client.go source directly.
confirmedFacts.evidence: c.con = &http.Client{Transport: c.Transport} -- no retryablehttp import, no retry/backoff fields on the Client struct, errors.Parse(body) returns immediately without retrying.

confirmedFacts.claim: terraform-provider-panos's go.mod lists `github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp v0.7.8 // indirect` -- i.e. it is pulled in transitively by some other dependency, not imported directly by the provider or by pango. Direct inspection of provider.go (client construction) shows no retryablehttp usage, RetryMax, CheckRetry, or backoff configuration -- the provider constructs a plain pango sdk.Client. This means the presence of go-retryablehttp in the dependency tree does NOT establish that terraform-provider-panos retries PAN-OS API calls on 429/5xx.
confirmedFacts.evidence: github.com/hashicorp/go-retryablehttp v0.7.8 // indirect  (line from raw go.mod, verified via direct curl, not LLM summary)

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-ansible (PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-ansible) depends on pan-os-python (>=1.13.1,<2.0) for all device communication per its requirements.txt, and does not implement its own retry/backoff around API calls in module_utils/panos.py. The only retry-like construct present is a connection-establishment timeout loop (retries PanDevice.create_from_device on PanDeviceError until a caller-supplied timeout elapses) -- this covers initial auth/connect failures only, not mid-operation 429/5xx responses, and there is no HTTP-status-code-aware retry logic anywhere in that file.
confirmedFacts.evidence: end_time = time.time() + timeout; while True: try: self.device = PanDevice.create_from_device(*pan_device_auth) except PanDeviceError as e: ... elif time.time() >= end_time: module.fail_json(...) -- connection-timeout retry only, no status-code branching, no backoff/sleep between attempts shown.

confirmedFacts.claim: Palo Alto Networks DOES implement standard HTTP 429 + rate-limit-header behavior on other, unrelated products in its portfolio -- e.g. the Threat Vault API (pan.dev) returns HTTP 429 with X-Minute-RateLimit-* / X-Day-RateLimit-* headers (200 req/min, 2000 req/day sliding window) and Prisma Cloud CSPM API documents its own rate-limit page -- proving Palo Alto has an established documentation pattern for rate limiting elsewhere, but neither of these is the PAN-OS/Panorama device-management XML or REST API this project targets, and neither uses Retry-After.
confirmedFacts.evidence: 'the API response returns the following code: 429, indicating that too many requests have been made' plus X-Minute-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset and X-Day-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset headers; no Retry-After header documented; Threat Vault is a separate cloud threat-intel service tied to Threat Prevention/Advanced Threat Prevention subscriptions, not the device management API.

confirmedFacts.claim: The project's own pan_api_research.md contains zero existing mentions of 429, retry, backoff, rate limiting, throttling, or concurrency anywhere in the file (grep for those terms returns no output), confirming the task's premise that this is a genuinely unaddressed gap in the project's prior research pass, not something already covered and merely uncited.

remainingGaps: Whether PAN-OS/Panorama's XML or REST API ever actually returns HTTP 429 with or without a Retry-After header under real load is UNCONFIRMED anywhere in official docs, pan.dev, or the three named open-source projects (pan-os-python, terraform-provider-panos/pango, pan-os-ansible) plus the underlying pan-python library. No official source documents ANY HTTP status code PAN-OS returns when the concurrency guidance ('limit to ~5 concurrent calls') is exceeded -- it is not stated whether exceeding it produces 429, 503, a slow/degraded response, a dropped connection, or no observable effect at all. This can only be settled by testing against a live device.

No official documentation states a recommended polling interval for async job status checks (log jobs, commit jobs) beyond the qualitative 'poll until status=FIN' instruction. The two default numbers found in this research (pan-python's 0.5s job-query interval; this project's own 3.0s default) are both unverified client-side choices, not Palo Alto guidance -- there is no official minimum-safe polling cadence documented.

Not confirmed whether the 'limit concurrent calls to ~5' guidance applies identically to the XML API (only the REST API getting-started page was found stating it verbatim; the XML API getting-started page returned 404 during this research pass and could not be independently checked for the same or a different number).

Could not exhaustively rule out retry/backoff logic existing somewhere else in pango's ~dozens of source files or in terraform-provider-panos's internal/ tree beyond client.go/provider.go and errors.go (errors.go 404'd) -- GitHub's code-search UI intermittently 429'd and then required sign-in during this session, so a full-repo grep for 'retryablehttp'/'429' usage inside pango was not completable; only a handful of files were read directly.

No LIVEcommunity (community.paloaltonetworks.com) forum thread reporting a real-world PAN-OS API 429 response was found in this pass -- searches surfaced only generic 429 content and PAN-OS docs pages, not an actual community report of the device returning 429. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence here; a targeted forum search from an authenticated session might surface more.

Whether PAN-OS's 'target=<serial>' Panorama-proxy path (querying a managed firewall through Panorama) has any different/tighter rate behavior than calling a firewall directly was not addressed anywhere found.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: The module docstring and both _get_with_retry (REST) and _xml_request (XML) currently treat 429-with-Retry-After and 5xx-exponential-backoff as if this were an established PAN-OS behavior 'mirrored from the Microsoft connector's base.py.' Research found NO official documentation and NO evidence in pan-os-python, pan-python, pango, terraform-provider-panos, or pan-os-ansible that PAN-OS/Panorama's XML or REST API ever returns HTTP 429 or a Retry-After header at all -- none of those official/community projects implement or even attempt to parse a 429 response from a PAN-OS device. Recommend: (1) relabel this code path's docstring/comments from an implicit 'confirmed pattern' to an explicit 'defensive/speculative: PAN-OS does NOT document 429/Retry-After behavior; this handles it opportunistically in case a load balancer, WAF, or Panorama proxy layer in front of the device emits it, but must not be presented as PAN-OS-documented behavior' -- update the 'Retry logic mirrors the Microsoft connector's base.py' docstring line (pan_base.py lines 19-21) accordingly. (2) The 5xx exponential-backoff branch is more defensible (PAN-OS REST error code 14 = 'Service unavailable' and code 4 = 'Gateway timeout' exist in the official error-codes table -- docs.paloaltonetworks.com/pan-os/11-1/.../pan-os-rest-api-error-codes -- these plausibly map to 503/504), but that mapping is still not spelled out with explicit HTTP status codes in the docs, so keep it flagged unconfirmed too, not promoted to 'confirmed'. (3) Add the officially-confirmed concurrency guidance (max ~5 concurrent API calls per docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/api/get-started-with-the-pan-os-rest-api) as an explicit client-side semaphore/limit if this connector is ever used concurrently across multiple evidence-collection tasks against the same host -- this is the one piece of real, citable Palo Alto guidance and the current code has no concurrency cap at all.

Add a new numbered section (e.g. '8. Rate Limiting, Retries, and Concurrency') documenting: (a) CONFIRMED -- official guidance to cap concurrent API calls at ~5 (docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/api/get-started-with-the-pan-os-rest-api), quoted verbatim; (b) NOT CONFIRMED / open gap -- no docs.paloaltonetworks.com, pan.dev, pan-os-python, pango/terraform-provider-panos, or pan-os-ansible source documents or implements a 429+Retry-After response/handling for PAN-OS's own XML/REST API (contrast with Palo Alto's OTHER products, Threat Vault and Prisma Cloud, which DO document 429 + rate-limit headers, to make clear this silence is specific to PAN-OS device management APIs, not a general Palo Alto documentation gap); (c) NOT CONFIRMED -- no official recommended job-status polling interval; note pan-python's own internal default of 0.5s vs this project's chosen 3.0s default in pan_base.py's _xml_log_retrieve, neither of which is Palo Alto guidance. Add this list to the existing 'Items That Must Be Confirmed Against a Live Suncoast Firewall Before Production Use' section (currently starting at line 104) so it isn't silently treated as settled.
